content_voiceover: This page has two clinical vignettes testing the 2022 classification updates. The first describes a 65 year old woman with pancytopenia, 16% myeloblasts, a TP53 mutation, a RUNX1 mutation, and translocation between chromosomes six and nine in most metaphases. Under ICC ELN 2022, the answer is AML with recurrent genetic abnormality. Translocation six nine, producing the DEK NUP214 fusion, is a defining lesion that classifies the case as AML even below the usual twenty percent blast threshold, and it takes priority over the co-occurring TP53 and RUNX1 mutations. The second vignette describes a 75 year old man with de novo AML on venetoclax and azacitidine, whose marrow shows trisomy eight, trisomy thirteen, loss of the Y chromosome, an NPM1 mutation, and FLT3 ITD with unknown allelic ratio. The correct answer is intermediate risk under ELN 2022. Loss of the Y chromosome is excluded from complex karyotype counting since it's often age related, leaving too few abnormalities for a complex karyotype. And under ELN 2022, the FLT3 ITD allelic ratio no longer changes the risk category for NPM1 mutated AML, so this combination lands in intermediate risk regardless.
keypoints: Translocation six nine with DEK NUP214 defines AML even under twenty percent blasts
Recurrent genetic abnormalities take priority over comutations like TP53 or RUNX1 for diagnosis
Loss of Y chromosome is usually excluded from complex karyotype counting
ELN2022 dropped FLT3-ITD allelic ratio as a risk modifier
NPM1 mutated plus FLT3-ITD is intermediate risk under ELN2022 regardless of allelic ratio
keypoint_voiceover: Two ELN2022 updates to memorize. First, defining recurrent genetic abnormalities like translocation six nine with DEK NUP214 establish an AML diagnosis even under the twenty percent blast cutoff, overriding co-mutations. Second, ELN2022 no longer uses the FLT3 ITD allelic ratio to set risk, so NPM1 mutated AML with FLT3 ITD is intermediate risk either way. And remember, isolated loss of the Y chromosome doesn't count toward a complex karyotype.
